reason: Conversation 1 latched onto a 'failing fan bearings' diagnosis that the ground truth lists as unsupported, told the homeowner to reach in and spin the internal cooling fan by hand (beyond the 'no opening hob' boundary), and ended by calling it a 'likely mechanical failure' despite the clear link to the new drawer. Conversation 2 correctly prioritised overheat protection from restricted ventilation after the drawer was fitted, asked for brand/model and the error code (and gave a practical tip to film the display), and when the homeowner refused DIY it offered sensible no-tools workarounds and the right escalation: get the fitter back to correct clearances, with Samsung support/engineer as the fallback if the hob itself is faulty. Its only weakness was stating the ventilation cause a little too confidently given the genuine uncertainty, but it still hedged toward a possible hob fault and never pushed parts.
